description: December 2023. Sajid Mir — convicted in May 2023 to 15 years for terror financing, the first real conviction of a 26/11 handler — is found poisoned in Central Jail, Dera Ghazi Khan. He is airlifted on ventilator support. The poisoning is unclaimed. Rizwan Shah's mission: determine whether the poisoning is an ISI internal operation (silencing a witness who may have begun cooperating with Indian intelligence via back-channels), a Dhurandhar operation (eliminating a target before Mir could cut a deal), or a factional LeT killing. The answer determines how to respond and whether Mir's intelligence value is now accessible.

real_world_correlation.real_status: Sajid Mir was convicted by a Pakistani anti-terrorism court in May 2023 (sentenced 15 years for terror financing). In December 2023, he was reportedly poisoned in Central Jail, Dera Ghazi Khan, and airlifted on ventilator support. The poisoning was unclaimed. His current health status as of 2026 is not publicly confirmed.
real_world_correlation.significance: Sajid Mir was the real-time coordinator of the 26/11 attacks — the voice on recordings coaching attackers in the Taj Hotel, Nariman House, and CST station. His conviction represented the first concrete Pakistan accountability for 26/11. His poisoning, if ISI-ordered, suggests ISI is cleaning house to prevent Mir from becoming an Indian intelligence witness. If Dhurandhar-ordered, it represents an operation that risked the rare accountability Pakistan had delivered.
real_world_correlation.india_interest: Indian intelligence would have had strong interest in Mir remaining alive — a living, convicted 26/11 handler in Pakistan's custody, potentially accessible via back-channels, is more valuable as an intelligence source than a dead one. His death (if it occurs) would eliminate the only institutionally-acknowledged 26/11 planner in Pakistan's custody.
real_world_correlation.who_benefits: ISI benefits from Mir's death — eliminates witness to internal coordination of 26/11. ISI's political cover benefits from Pakistan never having to extradite him. The LeT hardliners who view Mir's conviction as betrayal benefit. India does NOT benefit from his death — they want interrogation access.

mission_tasks.name: Attribute Mir poisoning: ISI internal, Dhurandhar external, or factional LeT
Assess whether Mir survives (intelligence value if yes: potential access via intermediary)
Map which ISI faction ordered poisoning — reflects internal 26/11 cleanup vs. new hardliner control

adversaries.objective: Eliminate Sajid Mir before he becomes an Indian intelligence asset or further embarrasses ISI through trial testimony

intelligence_targets.name: Identity of faction that ordered Sajid Mir's poisoning
What Mir may have told Pakistani investigators or international monitors about ISI 26/11 involvement
Which remaining 26/11 figures ISI may target to suppress evidence (Hafiz Saeed? Sajid Mir's co-conspirators?)
